_comment: PSMutant tested against ITSELF (dogfooding). Every source file is mutated except src/PSMutation.Sandbox.ps1, and that one exclusion is structural rather than a gap: its covering suite tests/Sandbox.Tests.ps1 calls Clear-PSMutationStaleSandbox for real, a self-mutation baseline runs IN-PROCESS so it shares $PID with the sandbox the run is executing from, and the sweep treats its own process id as reclaimable -- so naming that suite anywhere here deletes the live run's sandbox mid-baseline and turns the run red before a single mutant is tried. Its behaviour is pinned by the normal suite at 100% line coverage instead. NOTE: this exclusion previously cited a 'shared sandbox' (issue #2, since fixed) and then 'real temp side-effects', neither of which was the actual blocker. Run: Invoke-PSMutation -ConfigFile ./psmutant.self.config.json -SourceRoot .
_equivalentsComment: Mutants that provably cannot change behaviour, excluded from the denominator so the score means 'every catchable fault is caught'. Each needs a reason, and the run FAILS if one is ever killed or stops existing - a declaration is a checkable claim, not a mute button. Everything else here was killed by a test; nothing is listed merely because it was inconvenient. ONE DECLARATION RETIRED IN #3: `$isDeclared -> $true` in Get-PSMutationScore argued that counting undeclared keys into $matched could not be observed, because $matched is only read for keys that are declared. True when written. It stopped being true when the key became $null for an undeclared mutant -- $matched[$null] throws -- so the suite now kills all three of those mutants and the claim was removed rather than re-keyed. A declaration is a checkable claim, and this is what it looks like when one stops being needed.

equivalents.src/PSMutation.Report.ps1:Write-PSMutati: ConvertTo-Json -Depth N and -Depth N+1 emit byte-identical output for any object graph shallower than N. The report nests 4 deep at its worst (root -> mutants[] -> row -> scalar), so 6 and 7 cannot differ. Killing this would need a fixture built for no purpose but to out-nest the serializer, which would assert nothing about the report.
equivalents.src/PSMutation.Recheck.ps1:Write-PSMutat: Same as the Report.ps1 entry: the recheck report nests 4 deep at most (root -> mutants[] -> row -> scalar), so -Depth 6 and 7 serialise identically.
equivalents.src/PSMutation.Report.ps1:Get-PSMutation: An early return, not a decision. With $Equivalents null, $null.PSObject is null and so is .Properties, so the foreach below runs zero times and returns the same empty map the guard returns directly - verified by running the loop with the guard removed. Forcing the condition false therefore cannot change the output for any input. (Forcing it TRUE is killed: it would return an empty map even when declarations exist.)
